title: The spur first climbed and looked from
summary: Two sons of a shore household climb the spur above the southern lowland to look, and come back saying a man standing on its crown can see the whole lowland below him and any thing that moves across it long before it reaches the coast.

title: Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's wall dressed on its outer face only
summary: The mason who sets Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's first course dresses its stone smooth only where an enemy's eye might run along it, leaving the inner face raw, so that the wall stands smooth without and rough within through every season it is kept.

title: Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's gate hung
summary: A heavy oaken gate is hung on a socketed post at Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, its single doorway facing inland away from the sea, and swings shut of its own weight for the first time to the doubt of an old fisherman who mistrusts a door built facing from the water.

title: Cattle first driven up the spur
summary: Beasts used to level shore grazing are coaxed up the spur's steep ground for the first time, balking at the new gate, and settle within the wall to its thin grass within a few days of the climb.

title: The false watch on the lowland
summary: A boy of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raises the whole watch at dusk over shapes crossing the lowland from the west, taken for deer moving too evenly together; nothing is found by first light, and Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's watch is never again left to one pair of eyes.

title: The three rings begun on the height
summary: On a height near the south-eastern coast a crew begins the outer of three ringed walls under a woman said to read the ground before a stone is laid, a work on a scale no household of that coast has raised to before.

title: The cistern cut into the bedrock
summary: At the height's crown a basin is hollowed from the bedrock by heated stone cracked loose and cooled with water, a labour of two seasons that blisters more hands than the rest of the rings together.

title: The cistern first full
summary: The cistern fills for the first time from a spring the digging uncovers, and a child let down on a rope draws up the first measure, which the woman who read the ground tastes and says tastes of stone.

title: Cattle first driven inside the three rings
summary: Beasts are driven up the steeper climb into the three rings for the first time, more lost to loose scree on the way than the spur's own herders ever lost, and a woman who loses two of her own says the rings charge dear for what they let in.

title: The death of the woman who read the ground
summary: The woman who has read the ground for the three rings since the first course dies within the innermost ring at a great age and is buried there at her own asking, under a stretch of wall she named the soundest of her life.

title: The trodden way between the heights first paved
summary: A household along the worst stretch of the path between the spur and the height lays flat stones to keep its own feet dry, with no thought yet of any greater road, and others add paving of their own beside it.

title: The kerbing of the way spreads
summary: Upright stones set along the paving's edges hold it firm through a wet winter better than the unkerbed stretches beside it, and the practice spreads along the whole track within a few more seasons.

title: The first cart driven the whole way
summary: A cart of dressed stone drawn by two yoked oxen crosses the whole kerbed way for the first time without a wheel sinking to the axle, a day's haul where the same load once took the better part of three over open moor.

title: The last slab of the kerbed way laid
summary: The final slab of the track is set tilted rather than level on the last steep rise, and the small crew that lays it turns, its work done, to look inland toward the high pale country rather than back toward the sea.
